## How do I create an invoice?

<a id="create-invoice"></a>

Use Invoices to bill a customer who will pay you later. Saving the invoice records the sale and what the customer owes you.

**Where:** **Sales › Invoices** (`/invoices?new=1`)

1. Open Invoices and click "New Invoice" (Ctrl+I). → **Sales › Invoices** (`/invoices?new=1`)
2. Pick the customer, then add a line for each thing you sold: the item, quantity and rate.
3. Check the date, terms and total, then save. The amount now shows as owed by the customer.
4. To email or print it, save it marked to be emailed or printed, then use Print & Send Forms. → **Print & Send Forms** (`/invoices/send-forms`)

> Good to know: Paid on the spot? Use a Sales Receipt instead: no invoice is needed.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I create an invoice?", or ask Ask AI.*

## I got paid. How do I record it?

<a id="got-paid"></a>

It depends on whether you sent an invoice first.

**Where:** **Sales › Receive Payments** (`/payments?new=1`)

1. You sent an invoice: use Receive Payments, pick the customer, enter the amount and tick the invoices it pays. → **Sales › Receive Payments** (`/payments?new=1`)
2. No invoice (paid on the spot): use a Sales Receipt. → **Sales › Sales Receipts** (`/sales-receipts?new=1`)
3. When you take the money to the bank, use Make Deposits so your books show the same deposit as your bank statement. → **Banking › Make Deposits** (`/deposits?new=1`)

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "I got paid. How do I record it?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I record a sale that was paid right away?

<a id="sales-receipt"></a>

Use a Sales Receipt when the customer pays on the spot by cash, card or check, so no invoice is needed.

**Where:** **Sales › Sales Receipts** (`/sales-receipts?new=1`)

1. Open Sales Receipts and click "New Sales Receipt". → **Sales › Sales Receipts** (`/sales-receipts?new=1`)
2. Pick the customer, add what you sold and how they paid, then save.
3. Deposit the money with Make Deposits when it goes to the bank. → **Banking › Make Deposits** (`/deposits?new=1`)

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I record a sale that was paid right away?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I give a customer a quote and turn it into an invoice?

<a id="estimate-to-invoice"></a>

An estimate is a price quote. It does not change your books until you turn it into an invoice.

**Where:** **Sales › Estimates** (`/estimates`)

1. Open Estimates and click "New Estimate". Pick the customer, add the work or items and an expiration date, and send it to the customer. → **Sales › Estimates** (`/estimates`)
2. When the customer says yes, click Accept on the estimate, then "Convert to Invoice".
3. Billing in stages? Use "Create Progress Invoice" and bill a percentage of the estimate, or chosen quantities or amounts. The estimate keeps track of what is already invoiced and what remains.
4. Estimate Follow-up lists quotes that are still waiting for an answer. → **Admin › Estimate Follow-up** (`/estimates-followup`)

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I give a customer a quote and turn it into an invoice?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I give a customer a credit or a refund?

<a id="credit-memo-refund"></a>

A credit memo lowers what a customer owes you, for a return or a mistake. You can apply it to an invoice or refund the money.

**Where:** **Sales › Credit Memos** (`/credit-memos`)

1. Open Credit Memos and click "New Credit Memo". → **Sales › Credit Memos** (`/credit-memos`)
2. Pick the customer and add what you are crediting, then save.
3. On the credit memo, click "Apply Credit" to take it off an open invoice, or "Record Refund" to pay the money back from a bank account.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I give a customer a credit or a refund?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I see who owes me money, and follow up?

<a id="who-owes-me"></a>

The A/R Aging report shows each customer, what they owe and how late it is. Collect overdue payments is where you follow up.

**Where:** **A/R Aging** (`/reports/ar-aging`)

1. Open A/R Aging to see every customer balance by how overdue it is. → **A/R Aging** (`/reports/ar-aging`)
2. Open Collect overdue payments to log a call, email the overdue invoices or a statement, or print a collection letter. → **Sales › Collect overdue payments** (`/collections-center`)
3. Money coming in shows estimates, unbilled work, open and overdue invoices in one view. → **Sales › Money coming in** (`/income-tracker`)

> Good to know: You can also ask Ask AI "Who owes us money?" for the totals.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I see who owes me money, and follow up?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I send a customer a statement?

<a id="customer-statement"></a>

Customer Statement lists a customer’s charges, payments and balance for a period, one at a time or for every customer with a balance.

**Where:** **Customer Statement** (`/reports/statements`)

1. Open Customer Statement. → **Customer Statement** (`/reports/statements`)
2. Choose the Format (Balance Forward or Open Item), the customer and the dates, then view it.
3. For everyone at once, use "Batch — all customers with balances" and choose Combined PDF or ZIP (one PDF per customer).
4. To email one statement, use "Email a customer statement" on Print & Send Forms. → **Print & Send Forms** (`/invoices/send-forms`)

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I send a customer a statement?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I email or print invoices and other forms?

<a id="email-print-forms"></a>

Print & Send Forms holds everything marked "To be emailed" or "To be printed", so you send or print it in one go. Email needs your mail server set up once.

**Where:** **Print & Send Forms** (`/invoices/send-forms`)

1. Set up email once in Preferences > Send Forms (the mail server that sends your forms). → **Setup › Preferences** (`/settings`)
2. Open Print & Send Forms. → **Print & Send Forms** (`/invoices/send-forms`)
3. Under "To be emailed", tick the forms and click "Send selected". Under "To be printed", tick them and click "Print selected".

> Good to know: The name and address your forms are sent from, and "Bcc me", are in My Preferences.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I email or print invoices and other forms?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I add a customer or a job?

<a id="add-customer"></a>

Customers lists everyone you sell to, with their details, balance and history. A job is a project under a customer.

**Where:** **Sales › Customers** (`/customers`)

1. Open Customers and click "Add Customer". Fill in the name and contact details and save. → **Sales › Customers** (`/customers`)
2. For a project you track separately, add a job under the customer. → **Operations › Jobs** (`/jobs`)
3. Adding many at once? Use Add/Edit Multiple and paste them from a spreadsheet. → **Operations › Add/Edit Multiple** (`/lists/multiple`)

> Good to know: You can also type a new name straight into an invoice and add it from there.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I add a customer or a job?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I invoice many customers the same thing?

<a id="batch-invoice"></a>

Invoice many customers sends the same charge, for example a monthly fee, to a group of customers in one go.

**Where:** **Sales › Invoice many customers** (`/invoices/batch`)

1. Open Invoice many customers. → **Sales › Invoice many customers** (`/invoices/batch`)
2. Pick the customers (or a saved Billing Group) and add the items once.
3. Create the invoices, then send them from Print & Send Forms. → **Print & Send Forms** (`/invoices/send-forms`)

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I invoice many customers the same thing?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I charge late fees or interest?

<a id="late-fees"></a>

Late-payment charges adds interest or a late fee to customers whose invoices are overdue.

**Where:** **Sales › Late-payment charges** (`/finance-charges`)

1. Open Late-payment charges. → **Sales › Late-payment charges** (`/finance-charges`)
2. Check the rate and grace period, review the list, then assess the charges you want.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I charge late fees or interest?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I set up, charge and pay sales tax?

<a id="sales-tax"></a>

Add a sales tax item for each rate you charge and the agency it is paid to. Invoices and sales receipts then add the tax, and Pay Sales Tax sends what you collected to each agency.

**Where:** **Purchases › Pay Sales Tax** (`/sales-tax`)

1. Open Sales tax items and click "New sales tax item". Give it a name and a rate, and pick (or add) its tax agency. → **Accounting › Sales tax items** (`/sales-tax-components`)
2. Charge it on invoices and sales receipts. The Sales Tax Liability report shows what you owe each agency. → **Reports › Sales Tax Liability** (`/reports/sales-tax`)
3. To pay: open Pay Sales Tax, pick the bank account and the "show tax due through" date, tick the agencies and pay. → **Purchases › Pay Sales Tax** (`/sales-tax`)

> Good to know: Sales tax must be switched on in Preferences for these screens to show.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I set up, charge and pay sales tax?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I put my logo on invoices or change how they look?

<a id="invoice-template"></a>

Form Templates sets the logo, colors and fields on your invoices and other printed forms.

**Where:** **Setup › Form Templates** (`/templates`)

1. Open Form Templates. → **Setup › Form Templates** (`/templates`)
2. Pick the form, add your logo, choose the colors and the fields to show, then save.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I put my logo on invoices or change how they look?", or ask Ask AI.*
